fields.title: Horse Coat Colors
fields.short_description: Look at photos of horses and choose the correct coat color from the list. A great quiz to start with, especially if you’re new to the subject.

fields.question: What coat color is this?
fields.explanation: Chestnut horses have gray skin, and their coat color ranges from pale reddish gold to very dark reddish brown, almost black. They have no black ear rims, and the hair around the coronet bands is lighter.

fields.question: What coat color is this?
fields.explanation: Under the traditional Russian classification, igrénevaya is used only for draft horses, and the term itself is now outdated. The horse in the photo is a purebred Arabian. It cannot be palomino either, because Arabians do not carry the cream allele. Bays have a black mane and black ear rims. Here, “flaxen” refers to lightening of the mane and tail, and sometimes the legs.

fields.question: What coat color is this?
fields.explanation: More precisely, this is dapple gray. The horse’s base coat is still visible, and the body has lighter circular areas known as dapples. They are traditionally believed to reflect the pattern of the underlying blood vessels.

fields.explanation: Liver chestnut, also known as dark chestnut, can have a very dark coat like a dark bay or an almost black coat.
